correctness.rationale: Reran inputs/artifacts/certify.py independently: T1=0 nine-sums in S16 over C(16,9)=11440 subsets; T2=0 bad of 65 one-point extensions; T3=1832 nine-sums in S20 over C(20,9)=167960 subsets with no two disjoint; T4=0 bad of 61 extensions. Lemma C (g^2(H)<=g(H)+exp(H)) is proved by the standard two-step deletion argument and is sound. T4 reduction is valid because T3 certifies old zero-sums pairwise intersect, so any disjoint pair in an extension must use the new point; the script then exhaustively checks all (K-1)-subsets through the new point against old masks. Boundary conditions (distinctness, sizes 16/20, S16 subset S20, moduli 9, K=9) all assert and pass.

originality.rationale: Fused search (SerpBase/OpenAlex/Crossref/OpenAIRE) plus full fetch of the decisive k-Harborth paper (Lemos et al. arXiv:2209.14784) and Harborth literature shows no prior S16/S20, no C_9^2 two-fold bound, and no 1832-sum census. Bare inequality g(C_9^2)>=17 is implied by the 1983 Kemnitz elementary bound (n-1)2^{d-1}+1=17, which is disclosed and does not carry novelty; novelty rests on the explicit extension-maximal witnesses, the 1832-member pairwise-intersecting 9-sum family with no two disjoint, the g^2>=21 bound, and the 65/61 maximality sweeps, none of which is stated, tabulated, or implied by Kemnitz, Reiher/Gao prime-case theorems, C3xC3p results, or the differently-defined Lemos g^k (k-term, not k disjoint sums). No broader census, classification, or database covers C_9^2 disjoint 9-sums as a special case.

value.rationale: EMERGENT_FINDING genuinely arose from the target investigation: the p=3 base case of the admitted all-odd-p two-fold Harborth target, using the target's exact objects (9-term zero-sums in C_9^2, disjoint pairs), after the uniform Chevalley-Warning route stalled. The natural group C_9^2 and invariants g/g^2 were motivated before computation, exact values are not known, and the two-fold bound 21 materially advances the trivial bound 18 as the first rigorous foothold future all-p proofs must respect. The 1832-sum pairwise-intersecting census plus chain-maximality gives mathematical interpretation beyond unexplained enumeration, and Lemma C frames the exact-value problem via 21<=g^2<=g+9. DRAFT honestly disclaims exactness, p>=5, classification, and Chevalley-Warning, so the narrow exact witness is judged on its own per STANDARD without demanding a general theorem.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Lemos et al. Theorem 3.11/Prop 3.4 concern g^k = smallest l with a k-term zero-sum in a set (k=3,4,6,8 over Cp/Cn/C2^r); Kemnitz lower-bound construction is an existential size-17 witness class, not the coordinates of S16/S20, not the 1832 census, not maximality sweeps. Lemma C (g^2<=g+exp) is elementary two-step deletion and is framed as auxiliary, not the headline novelty.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior work implies at most the bare number 17 via parameter substitution n=9,d=2 into Kemnitz, which is why bare (A)-number alone is not novel; it does not imply the specific S20 disjointness property, the exact count 1832 with pairwise intersection, the 61-extension maximality, or g^2>=21, because those involve disjoint pairs of 9-sets, a different predicate from any prior k-term theorem. Hence the headline is not a recomputation, corollary, or repackaging of a known stronger fact.
